# Actors Resource Assurance — Research Conclusions

## Ownership and Evidence Status

This is the single compiled owner of exploratory Actors resource-assurance conclusions. It is **not an Experiment Record**, a production price or a second backlog. [EXP-001](EXP-001.md) owns the physical baseline; [BACKLOG](../../../../../BACKLOG.md) owns open work. Specifications, code and tests retain project-owned truth. No build, test, CI or production acceptance operation depends on this document.

Raw receipt pages, their historical snapshot and the companion manifest are intentionally not retained. The observations below are reviewed, source-scoped conclusions, not a self-contained audit/replay dataset. Artifact identities distinguish the original coordinates; they do not make old measurements current. New production qualification must use applicable code and adequate current evidence, not this summary as a substitute for raw data.

## Saturation Frontier and Admission Scope

The [performance specification §6a](../../../../../docs/deos/actors-performance-assurance.specification.en.md#6a-saturation-frontier-and-user-admission-acceptance) owns the predictive/acceptance contract; [resource policy §7.1](../../../../../docs/deos/actors-resource-policy.specification.en.md#71-network-wide-user-admission) owns reference admission constraints. P28-28 in BACKLOG owns execution and release closure. This section compiles applicability and implementation constraints, not another model, measurement runner, Experiment or task queue.

| Retained coordinate | Admissible reuse | Not established |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T1 first-block Transfer76/63; R2 Router50/44 | Distinct first-wave snapshots; exact identities/costs in [Best Verified Results](experiments.md#best-verified-results) | Matched A/B, stationary throughput or admission threshold |
| System/User1024 recurring Transfer | Fixed64+100 windows, insufficient warmup/source-limited coverage; existing runner and fees/custody checks | Sustainable maximum or freely extended warmup |
| Original128-block Deadline target | Retain targetMet=false and observed lateness | Completion promoted from censoring |
| Separate quiet Deadline sweep | Native1024returns/terminal retries; [source/log and booked costs](experiments.md#native-deadline-diagnostic-coordinate) | Useful economic throughput, original target repair or physical qualification |
| H1/H2/H3 and W0–W12 | Reuse actual workload/branch/geometry and finite source-qualified evidence | Complete physical P/R, target transfer or whole-domain stability |

**Verified source boundary:** do_create_user_actor checks the global breaker and User creation switch. Both new-identity paths now check the qualified user_identity_capacity(current_authority) port against projected total identities before payment/allocation and recheck fresh authority/count before committing; Active creation also retains population and per-Contract maximum fit. do_activate_actor retains dormant identity and does not consult the new-identity switch. Existing Contract replacement has its own fit check. None is a network sustainable-throughput certificate. ActorIdentityCount and ActiveActorCount are bounded population counters; Service header count includes ineligible/already-considered residents and cannot stand in for eligible arrivals or age. The frozen resource meter/telemetry is a block resource owner/projection, not a history of demand.

**Structural model implication:** Latching, one open Run and busy-period discard can bound on-chain queues while offered recurring demand remains underserved. Predictions must separate offered history (often unavailable on chain), accepted latch/eligibility, per-stage reentry and actual retirement from S/A and successful effects. FIFO/Q1 can bound encounter order without guaranteeing a useful market effect; unavailable collection/markets and repeated refusals belong in explicit failure assumptions and censored outcomes. No positive physical service curve or numerical sustainable frontier is accepted here.

**Pass-count falsifier:** scheduler.rs::execute_cycle_to_cutoff_inner initializes executed/scanned locally; lib.rs calls the resource-aware worker in both Prepass and Drain, sharing resource/round state. The new minimal native test saturation_count_ceiling_is_per_pass_not_sustainable_block_capacity executes PASS through scoped ci-local: six System Actors with two-Step Transfer plans, mock per-pass cap3, two passes at B2 each advance three distinct Actors; the third cannot consume their second owed Steps. Two B3 passes complete them, preserving FIFO, Q1, B+1 and twelve exact debit/credit effects. It uses existing builders/mock declarations/Weight::MAX, not the production allocator, timing, witness or capacity. No best-performance row is created from this count-geometry regression. Executed test sourced12321f4be20d0dea1dd18cf13bf5003626d9ece6b7f056635cee5114903f779, mockb046eef4 and unchanged scheduleraefc7706 bind the native coordinate. Scoped default tests, workspace/all-target/all-feature Clippy, format and scoped completion pass; no runtime/physical campaign is rerun and production Weight/Wasm/metadata/lock pins stay unchanged.

**Implemented native subset / qualification constraint:** The existing identity count now reserves full legal future activation potential at new identity admission, not only current Active demand. A conservative uniform identity-credit ceiling can reuse ActorIdentityCount, counting dormant identities as potential credits rather than overloaded work. That avoids a new ledger and avoids revoking existing dormant activation or legal replacement/recovery paths. A workload-specific bound cannot silently qualify arbitrary future Contracts. System authority remains independent; overdraw prevents further User creation, not existing service. The ordinary switch remains a separate necessary condition. Production must stay unavailable until a code/configuration-bound whole-domain ceiling and complete creation/lookup owner are justified; no positive number is inferred from the historical rows.

**Policy/fee disposition:** Normal and hard refusal plus atomic credit acquisition/release may be sufficient; Constrained/utilization hysteresis and surcharges remain proposed. Credit recovery on actual identity destruction avoids noisy utilization feedback; deactivation cannot surrender retained activation authority. Keep the existing Creation Fee/collection/holds unchanged and make refusal payment-neutral apart from ordinary transaction fees. New consensus counters, per-Actor creation scans, off-chain forecast authority and fee-purchased priority are rejected. The native source implements this reservation/refusal/recovery subset. Reconciled gate/source reviews and named profile/API results below close their bounded scopes only; complete physical/artifact and production qualification remain open. P0-B host refusal and P0-C physical P/R/target applicability are unchanged.

**Supported source lemma:** The local tool passes DEFAULT_BACKING_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT into ValidationContext.exec_timeout and selects PvfExecKind::Backing. In PVF36 execute/worker_interface.rs, start_work takes that same timeout; handle_result maps an otherwise successful WorkerResponse with duration>T to JobTimedOut. ## Proof Input-Budget Conditional Native Component

**Decision and consumer:** The P0-C/P28-19 one-axis method slice now has an executable conditional checker in `template/tools/pvf-validation/src/proof_input_budget.rs`, registered only under cfg(test). This is neither another physical experiment nor a complete execution-profile method: it implements the sufficient original-hash/weight premise without copying the private Cumulus recorder, adding dependencies, changing production paths or replaying closed pilots. The [package entrypoint](../../../../../template/tools/pvf-validation/README.md#hash-owner-input-budget-prototype) owns usage and current implementation scope; BACKLOG.md owns applicability and complete-owner work.

**Supported conditional model:** For supplied decoded proof P plus implicit V1 null [0], let b(h) be the maximum supplied SCALE byte-vector weight under original Blake2 hash h. Both each conversion and U=sum b(h) are checked against u32::MAX. ## Authorship No-Author Entry-Domain Reduction

**Question:** May complete Authorship qualification drop discovery returning None because Aura always supplies an author? Only under a named entry/profile and explicit coherence premises. The registered Cumulus validation entry and direct Executive/runtime APIs are not the same boundary. This is source reduction, not a native accepted-block witness or a network-admission defect.

| Source branch | Authorship consequence | Exclusion boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cached Author exists | Return cached account, then invoke callback | Canonical cold-cache lineage is separate from this generic supported path |
| No Aura pre-runtime item, first matching item fails Slot decoding, or Aura authority count decodes as zero | Aura FindAuthor returns None | AuraExt seal verification requires Some index before executing the block |
| Aura index exists but Session.Validators lacks that index | Session adapter returns None | AuraExt verifies an Aura key, not this separate account mapping; require roster coherence |
| Cold discovery returns None | No cache creation or callback; on_initialize still returns zero and on_finalize still kills cache | Zero return or absent callback declaration does not make discovery/wrapper/deletion free |

**Actual entry chain:** `runtime/src/lib.rs:276` registers AuraExt BlockExecutor for validate_block. ParachainSystem `validate_block/implementation.rs:251–271` invokes `E::verify_and_remove_seal` before `E::execute_verified_block`, in separate externalities/recorder scopes. AuraExt `lib.rs:132–174` requires one decodable Aura seal, a Some Aura author index, an indexed cached authority and successful signature verification. No index exits by panic before the Authorship hook. This guard has its own incurred-work/host owner; source placement supplies no CPU, witness discount or proof-floor bound.

**Narrow conditional exclusion:** The verified header's first Aura input must survive to Authorship, its Aura authority count must remain the same, and the selected index must exist in Session.Validators. Under these premises the configured Session adapter returns Some, so cold no-author is excluded. Current source supports the coherence argument: named genesis uses the same invulnerable sequence for Session keys; ordinary TrustedSet management returns Some roster; rotation installs validators from session_keys and Aura receives those keys. Truncation and the empty-update no-op have different consequences; the [empty-queue countercase](#authorship-empty-queue-coherence-countercase) defeats a general roster-coherence inference. Authorship precedes ordinary rotation. First rotation/queued-change, earlier cache/digest/roster mutation, upgrade/LP histories and actual executing-entry binding must stay explicit; this record does not certify their complete reachable-state induction or a generic-host invariant.

**Broader entry limit:** `apis.rs:230–235` delegates Core execute/initialize directly to Executive. Executive's ExecuteBlock seal method is empty; its initialization extracts pre-runtime digests and runs hooks without the AuraExt wrapper. Aura on_initialize tolerates missing/undecodable slot input by its no-update branch. Timestamp checks stored-slot consistency later, and the consensus hook checks relay-slot alignment later; neither is an entry-local proof that Authorship already returned Some. Thus no-author cannot be excluded from all initialization/API/helper attempts using the PVF guard. No successful whole block, admitted parent lineage or bypass of full validation is established here.

**Method decision:** Keep author-discovery None distinct from an absent recipient account: c=0/1/2 all prepare successful discovery. A future complete quote must either bind the narrower verified/coherent profile with its premises, or supply supported coverage/domination for retained None branches on both axes. Do not automatically add a fixture or promote successful-discovery timings to a no-author maximum. Seal validation, Authorship body/callback/wrapper and retained finalization need explicit non-duplicated owners; exact registered-prefix arithmetic does not prove their charge sufficiency. Native c=2 remains accepted without replay or rebinding.

## Authorship Empty-Queue Coherence Countercase

**Question/result:** Does ordinary TrustedSet source preserve the roster premise needed to exclude no-author? Not generally. The narrow conditional theorem above remains valid, but its coherence premise cannot be inferred merely from ordinary mode or shared Session/Aura handling. Aura `change_authorities(empty)` explicitly returns without updating Authorities. Session can install an empty validator vector before invoking that handler. This is a source-backed transition countercase, not an executed valid block, public ancestry, exploit or price.

**Source profile:** Without `runtime-benchmarks`, `configs/staking_config.rs:53–63` returns TrustedSet unconditionally; LP fixture key/read is compiled only with that feature. Session's native scheduler is NeverEndSession; RuntimeSessionRotation supplies periodic rotation after Authorship. Named genesis supplies keys for the same invulnerable identities used by the manager. Its genesis calls for epochs0/1 read the same roster, and default QueuedChanged is false. Benchmark fixture writes and runtime upgrades are not premises of this countercase.

Let L be a nonempty initial invulnerable list, K its Aura keys, V the active Session validator vector, Q queued pairs and C QueuedChanged. Keep invulnerables unchanged and let every member sign the existing `Session::purge_keys` call. It removes NextKeys/key ownership and releases key custody references; it does not mutate V, Q or active Aura keys. Runtime BaseCallFilter does not deny that call. This source path requires authorized signer participation, not arbitrary deletion of another validator's keys.

| Transition | V / Aura | Q / C | Decisive source behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Named genesis | L / K | pairs(L,K) / false | Manager genesis0/1 return the same keyed invulnerables |
| Signed purge of every NextKeys entry | L / K | unchanged / false | Purge affects future key loading, not already queued/current sets |
| First rotation | L / K | empty / true | Activate old Q; manager returns Some(L), all load_keys fail, next_changed starts true |
| Second rotation | empty / K | empty / true | Install empty Q into V; changed=true handler passes empty keys, Aura ignores the update |

**First-rotation distinction:** Initial C=false does not itself create this mismatch: genesis Q still activates the same validators/keys even after NextKeys is purged. The first rotation prepares empty Q with C=true because TrustedSet returns Some(L). The second rotation exposes the empty-update exception. Generic QueuedChanged=false/key-upgrade histories are not silently certified by this example.

**No-author consequence:** AuraExt finalization copies retained K, and its next validation guard can find an index/key from K; it does not read V. Cold Session-backed author lookup then sees V empty and returns None. Aura disabled checks read the disabled-index collection, not a nonempty V invariant. This identifies why seal/index validation alone cannot prove account discovery. No complete header/relay-proof/state-root replay was performed; remaining block/context checks and earlier cache/digest state retain their own obligations. The source transition falsifies broad coherence preservation without asserting that a particular full block has been admitted.

**Evidence-selected correction:** Preserve the accepted conditional entry-domain reduction and c=2 observations at their original scopes. Narrow its supporting roster argument: shared Session handling is insufficient at the empty update. Complete ordinary-domain Authorship qualification must retain None behavior or justify a stronger actually enforced admission premise; an unshipped nonempty-queue rule or assumed collator key health is not such a premise. No pricing or economic/consensus behavior change is authorized here.

**Next evidence boundary:** A default-native source-transition control should invoke actual signed-origin purge, two real reference rotation calls and cold Authorship lookup, asserting V/Q/Aura/callback/cache/finalization consequences without raw roster injection or a fabricated long chain. Such a control is not complete validation or a physical campaign. Do not repeat old c=0/1/2 or host controls merely for confidence; admit new execution only for this exposed transition. P28-19 remains the sole open-work owner.

## Authorship Phase-Composition Source Feasibility

**Accepted direction and scope:** One complete logical Authorship owner, with separately qualified initialization/finalization phases, is accepted for method design. This pass inspects existing APIs and carriers only; it implements no driver, fixture, measurement, coefficient or artifact. It does not mark the pricing method Prepared. Current source baseline contains the accepted c=2 and empty-queue controls; their observations are reused, not rerun.

| Surface | Source result | Method consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing three Authorship extras | `Config::execute` runs initialization and finalization adjacently; wider variants add System initialization/root | No existing late-finalization stage or intervening-context model |
| Native Recording port | Public BenchmarkRecording invokes its supplied callback before proof/time start; existing host tests already use custom callbacks | Possible native prefix-before-window mechanism, not an implemented phase driver |
| Generated v2 runner | Owns its callback, commits setup, prefills whitelist and resets DB counters before start; one marked body per instance | A finalizer prepared in ordinary setup would be committed as original state; no ready stock phase route |
| Overlay/recorder lifecycle | Ext commit drains overlay changes; benchmark backend reopens and resets recorder/root; DB counter reset only wipes trackers | Commit/reset cannot be treated as a harmless pause between phases |
| Default timing implementation | SDK host uses SystemTime since UNIX epoch; elapsed uses saturating subtraction | Time observation, not CPU or a monotonic/conservative upper certificate; selected binary/host still needs attestation |
| Proof coordinate | Benchmark backend can report compact encoded proof size; Cumulus size-only recorder sums newly seen encoded inputs | Two phase increments cannot simply become a full-owner bound or transfer numerically between hosts |
| Post-body work | v2 stops recording, then commits changes, then times a separate root call | Adding extrinsic_time and storage_root_time does not cover the untimed commit; wider root diagnostics are not complete later commit ownership |
| Wasm route | Current Benchmark API delegates config/whitelist to generated batches; no separate phase carrier is exposed | Native port feasibility is not an ordinary-Wasm/host bridge |

Calling instance twice is not sufficient: each existing instance reruns its fixture setup.

**Workflow skeleton:** One last prepared-parent commit establishes R0 before the preparation prefix. Derive/authenticate root/layout on an isolated setup peer from the immutable parent; construct the primary host independently from that identical committed Storage, binding the constructor/layout identity and subsequent proof-backed replay. Do not run a preparatory root/readback probe on the primary or share warmed caches from the setup peer. The cold-primary R0 binding is a mechanism obligation, not an already implemented check. No in-gap root query is a harmless assertion; matching root hashes alone cannot authenticate a recorder reset or unchanged-root commit.

```text
committed native parent / authenticated R0
  -> declared component prefix
  -> I.begin -> actual single-pallet Executive wrapper -> I.end
  -> declared nonempty native gap and source-scoped retain/drop points
  -> F.begin -> actual Authorship finalization -> F.end
  -> freeze owned read-witness result
  -> separately labelled root/repair probe -> freeze transition-witness result
  -> independent verification/replay; never feed probes back into earlier phases
```

**Domain and lifetime boundary:** Reuse the source-proven successful-discovery and actual key-purge/two-rotation transition recipes, not raw roster injection or invented ancestry. The default-only test is cfg-excluded from the proposed profile; its passed four cells remain semantic evidence, not execution of this host. A first mechanism scope can use successful discovery with an existing funded recipient and None; it does not cover all c/d states or target branches. Bind setup, gap operands, allocation owners and drop points explicitly. Do not retain the old combined Fixture/Digest until F merely for convenience, or prematurely release header/digest/buffer allocations. Full Executive prefix, remaining initialization, external/idle context and target lifetime equivalence are still unbound; refuse any corresponding full-domain claim.

**Observer separation:** The primary witness workflow must not run H1 Sample, whole-state snapshots, Authorship::author readback, account/counter probes or arbitrary verification between boundaries. H1 `snapshot()` iterates TOP via next_key/get, and Sample calls it before/after observation; absence of a tracing subscriber does not disable a proof-enabled backend recorder. Those reads can donate original inputs and warming outside the claimed phase. This is a combination hazard, not invalidation of existing TestExternalities logical controls. Use a fresh diagnostic peer from the identical parent/inputs, never sharing recorder/cache state; compare its transition with an unprobed reference and primary workflow. Close proof copies before later verification can taint a live recorder handle. The H1 4096-key limit remains its diagnostic limit, not a new protocol cap.

**Witness/root ownership:** B/E observations are backend diagnostics, not Cumulus matching-unit bounds. Compact-size fallback0 and unchecked SDK u32 casts must not silently certify empty work or exact conversion. Freeze the read-witness result at F end, then label any subsequent actual root materialization separately: it may reveal original repair inputs missing from the earlier read proof. Replaying a captured read proof alone does not establish mixed-delta completeness. The whole prefix/gap/root witness may be a conservative superset; it is not automatically an Authorship-owned U_W or a charged ProofSize projection. Exact root/state-version, original-input membership, required repair and matching-consumer adapters remain implementation/qualification gates.

**Replay adapter boundary:** `create_proof_check_backend` checks root presence in the supplied node database, not complete read/mutation/repair coverage. Its successful construction is not replay success. Actual reads and the mixed root transition must run; the pinned Ext expects backend reads not to fail. Missing-proof/backend failure must reject the claimed replay, never become None/default/success or an unclassified expected panic. A targeted refusal needs a valid positive peer and authenticated required-input premise.

**Root-error boundary:** Pinned SDK `sp-state-machine-0.54.0/src/trie_backend_essence.rs:629–657` catches a delta-trie-root error, logs a warning and returns the original root with its write overlay, without requiring a panic. Source SHA-256 `96dc0d1ac010b23f92c64c2b08ebca5ba0cc48ac7a43f4d8509b9bd343801c8e`. Successful API return, absence of panic or readable overlay post-state is not successful root repair.

**Independent reference:** Authenticate the expected mixed post-state/root using a separate valid full-state reference under identical parent, layout, inputs and transitions, not the same incomplete proof or mutually matching old roots. Reject any root/transition mismatch or classified backend failure. A repair-specific negative must establish its required repair-input premise and use a validated root-changing reference case so the old-root fallback cannot pass; if it fails earlier on an original read, that establishes only the narrower read-refusal claim. Legitimate net-zero transitions may retain R0; unchanged root is not universally invalid. If the repair premise or independent check cannot be established, retain an unsupported result rather than claim repair completeness.

A candidate family is a separate conservative phase/branch envelope over explicitly bounded source/context operands; c/d remain categorical labels, not assumed linear regressors. Digest/roster/cache/economic states, late overlay/allocator context, caller glue, clock coordinate and host applicability must support that family before calibration. Source bounds and a variability/error argument are missing, not zero or guessed constants. Keep U_I/U_F separate from the complete matching-unit U_W obligation; no coefficients, maxima, timing samples, quarter headroom or reserve credit follow from this mapping.

**Common-work boundary:** The proposed root probe establishes only the declared native transition. It does not qualify root/commit/persistence/validation/System costs or waive them from the complete ownership map. Do not commit the primary overlay between I/F; any later persistence belongs to an explicit separate scope. A future inclusive binding must retire the invoked callback charge once, preserve its None-path absence, and avoid duplicating prepaid F in outstanding R under the one freeze. These remain project-contract requirements, not new fees or counters.

## Authorship Retained-Scope Collector Method Decision

**Question and decision scope:** Can the accepted no-clock carrier become a complete physical Authorship method on the selected SDK without losing original inputs or adding production observers? Select one candidate: a custom, off-chain native retained-scope collector around actual I/F calls, with checked raw clock endpoints and a complete-witness projection into the target consumer's units. Status is Proposed / Not Prepared, not a selected implementation or collection campaign. The [Phase-Driver Contract](../../../../../docs/deos/actors-performance-assurance.specification.en.md#authorship-phase-driver-contract) owns requirements; this note owns the concrete candidate and its source-supported refusals. No new Experiment or best-result row is warranted.

**Baseline:** Reuse the closed [native cohort](#authorship-bounded-no-clock-native-result) and [SDK reassessment](#sdk-patch-native-evidence-reassessment); do not rerun either. The [SDK dependency owner](../../../../../docs/deos/actors.integration.en.md#sdk-dependency-line) owns current graph/artifact/client identities and their bounded approval. Its issued ordinary artifact removes the earlier artifact-absence prerequisite, not the clock, complete-domain or executing-host transfer gaps. The no-clock module remains test-only under ordinary runtime-benchmarks, excluding authority scaffolding; it is neither a default-native nor a Wasm collector.

| Collector boundary | Selected design | Admission/refusal condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parent and host | One authenticated R0/layout, one BenchmarkingState plus Ext/OverlayedChanges per workflow; setup peer is independent | Bind source-consistent prefix, allocation owners and retention; refuse child-state or context outside supported capture |
| I | Read raw start endpoint, invoke actual single-pallet Executive registration wrapper once, read raw end endpoint | Preserve discovery/cache, callback and registration; no combined adjacent I/F helper |
| Gap | Execute declared intervening transitions on the same host/overlay/recorder | No commit, reopen, wipe, recorder reset, whitelist prefill or verification; native transfer1ED remains only a finite mechanism recipe |
| F | Read raw start endpoint, invoke actual finalization once, read raw end endpoint; freeze owned read witness | Preserve None deletion and supported late context; equal compact endpoints grant no free F |
| Transition and verification | Separately label root/repair inputs, freeze complete witness, then independent full-state/proof-only verification | No observer donation; silent old-root fallback must fail against an independent reference; root/commit time is not silently included in F |

**Time family, not a fitted price:** Choose a branchwise constant conservative envelope, not a c/d regression. Let b identify a source-derived co-reachable discovery/cache, callback-result and late-residence branch, with its full admitted context domain D_b. Each branch needs quantitative source/applicability bounds for digest/roster payloads, ledger/event state, earlier cache users and late overlay/allocation context. Finite fixture labels do not establish those bounds; no new domain cap or worst-state ordering is assumed. A branch partition or context bound not yet justified leaves the family unsupported.

```text
p in {I, F}; b ranges over source-supported co-reachable branches
obs_ns[p] = checked_sub(raw_end_ns[p], raw_start_ns[p])
obs_ps[p] = checked_mul(obs_ns[p], 1000)
U_p(b) = checked_add(theta_p,b, error_p,b, transfer_p,b)   [integer ps]
U_phase = max_b checked_add(U_I(b), U_F(b))
```

**Clock and calibration meaning:** The selected raw endpoint source is public SDK current_time(), UNIX-epoch nanoseconds, not CPU time or a monotonic clock. Keep u128 endpoints/conversions exact; reject missing endpoints, backward endpoint order, overflow and zero/unresolved-resolution observations rather than saturating. Hidden clock adjustments, variability/underfit and measurement-boundary effects still need a supported error enclosure; endpoint checks alone do not supply it. theta is the prospective native model coefficient, error its conservative enclosure, and transfer a separately justified ordinary-Wasm/host upper for code, optimization, context and lifetime differences. None is supplied, guessed or assumed zero. Before calibration, support D_b, the error policy and the transfer; later coefficients must reject any supported-domain undercoverage after that treatment. A raw maximum/percentile is not theta.

**Why not reuse two BenchmarkRecording rows:** SDK BenchmarkRecording keeps endpoints private, uses SystemTime and returns saturating differences; its elapsed field alone cannot distinguish a backward clock from zero work. The public raw clock permits the proposed checked adapter, but supplies no discontinuity/resolution bound. The generated runner additionally commits/prefills before start, commits after stop, then separately times root; it cannot be used as this retained-phase driver. No code for the custom adapter is implemented here.

**One complete proof projection:** Target the selected Cumulus SizeOnlyRecorder input-byte coordinate, not compact proof, PoV or an execution price. For a complete witness W, index encoded node/external-value blobs by their content hash under the same hasher/layout/codec. Define Q(W) as the checked sum of SCALE encoded_size(blob) once per content identity. This includes each blob's SCALE length prefix; it is neither sum(raw lengths), the encoded size of the proof container nor the benchmark backend's compact size. Cumulus charges NodeOwned after NodeCodec encoding, EncodedNode and external Value only on first seen hash; Hash/NonExisting/InlineValue bookkeeping adds no separate blob bytes.

**Conditional matching argument:** An owner-scope newly charged size-only input count is at most Q(W) only if every target-counted encoded blob is covered by W and the shared seen-set/lifetime, codec and widths match. Inherited baseline grants no subtraction credit; this does not bound an unrelated absolute end counter. Required read/absence/mutation/repair input inclusion must be authenticated at R0 and against the mixed transition, with independent full-state/root comparison and required-input removal falsifiers. Native replay of the two cases is not coverage of all target contexts. A prefix/gap/root superset may be conservative only after that target-inclusion proof. Q(W) is a per-case projection, not yet a domain upper U_W; the method also needs a justified bound over every D_b. Compact B/E increments are diagnostics only and never inputs to Q or a complete-witness sum.

| Work ownership | Candidate treatment | Remaining qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Discovery/cache/callback/registration | Inside I, including None's performed discovery and wrapper work | Full admitted branch/context and target transfer |
| Actual cache deletion | Inside F, including absence and late overlay residence | Full late-context/lifetime and input coverage |
| Repair/root/commit/persistence/validation/System glue outside I/F | Assign each source operation once to an explicitly qualified common owner, or refuse the incomplete owner map | No qualified common coverage is established here; the native root probe is not a physical owner |
| Inclusive binding | Retire contained callback charge once, respecting its None-path absence; do not reserve prepaid F again in R | Future qualified binding only; no fee, coefficient, P/R provider or reserve change |

**Readiness verdict:** Not Prepared. The design fixes a clock protocol, model family, witness projection and ownership boundaries, but source feasibility is not supported physical applicability. The first blocking time cell is a justified clock/error plus native-to-ordinary upper: neither raw SDK clock nor accepted native carrier/issued Wasm supplies it. Separately, complete D_b bounds, target blob inclusion/domain U_W and qualified common work remain open. U_phase is not a complete owner price while those exclusions are unqualified. More native points cannot close a missing transfer or domain premise.

**Smallest reopening evidence:** A source-selected executing-host/entry route with a conservative clock/error and native-to-target domination argument over the named D_b; alternatively direct target execution would be a newly selected method, not a quiet fallback in this one. Any later implementation/build/calibration needs separate selection after its applicable method prerequisites. Required rejection checks are backward/zero/overflow clock inputs, unsupported branch/late state, real lifecycle reset/commit, original-input removal, silent root fallback and a target counted blob absent from W. Reuse existing mechanism falsifiers only within their accepted scope; hypothetical checks above were not executed. No benchmark-Wasm, tool installation, sample, coefficient, pricing or production acceptance follows.

## Authorship Direct-Wasm Carrier Feasibility

**Verdict and scope:** The existing exact-artifact Core_execute_block route is source-feasible as a complete ordinary-Wasm execution carrier with retained I/gap/F context. It is not an Authorship phase-resolved collector: the inspected artifact and harness expose no supported complete I/F observation boundary. This closes one read-only source/static feasibility question, not implementation, calibration, a complete physical method or production acceptance. It neither replaces the [native candidate](#authorship-retained-scope-collector-method-decision) silently nor proves every possible off-chain VM observer impossible. No such observer is selected here.

**Exact artifact inspection:** Reuse ordinary Wasm SHA-256 2df308749408946a7b4ad6f90b3d5aabca8defe1fa03c7c11806fac409ccb8d9 from the [SDK owner](../../../../../docs/deos/actors.integration.en.md#sdk-dependency-line). A prior read-only inspection hash-checked its 1534579 compressed bytes, decompressed the SDK-prefixed Zstd blob and walked complete Wasm import/export sections: 7691008 decompressed bytes, 43 imports and 49 exports. Node26.8.1 used built-in Zstd with the SDK's 50MiB inspection bomb limit; it performed no WebAssembly compilation, instantiation or execution. These are artifact-layout facts, not resource measurements. This documentation pass reuses that inspection rather than rerunning it.

| Inspected surface | Source/static result | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Runtime exports | Core_execute_block, Core_initialize_block and BlockBuilder apply/finalize/check/inherent entrypoints exist; no Authorship phase or Benchmark export | Complete block execution is callable; no direct per-owner API boundary |
| Runtime imports | No tracing/benchmarking/timestamp/current_time import; proof-size hostfunction import exists | A host tracing subscriber cannot recover absent Wasm tracing calls; proof observations are not phase timestamps |
| Execution route | wasm_replay.rs uses WasmExecutor, explicit supplied code binding and Core_execute_block; apis.rs delegates to Executive | No native execution fallback in this route; source feasibility is not a new successful replay |
| I/gap/F lifetime | One execution recorder, backend, overlay and Ext surround one runtime export call; Executive runs initialization, extrinsics/idle and finalization inside it | No harness-inserted commit/reopen/reset between Authorship I/F; actual runtime transactions remain part of the workflow |
| Root/verification | System finalization occurs inside final_checks; host drain_storage_changes follows the export; binding/inherent checks and proof-only replay use separate recorder scopes | Root/repair and host tails remain explicit; no complete owner price or witness bound follows |

**Boundary obstruction:** FRAME generates hook spans around Hooks::on_initialize and Hooks::on_finalize, but no_std tracing macros are no-ops without their tracing feature and the issued artifact has no tracing imports. Source-level span names alone do not provide a live observation channel. Independently, Executive calls register_extra_weight_unchecked after the on_initialize hook returns, outside its hook span; observing only that span would still omit owning I registration/glue. The current helper's external execute/return boundary is whole-block, not complete Authorship I/F.

**Rejected shortcuts:** Timing the whole Core_execute_block call would include other initialization, extrinsics, idle, finalization and executor work; no matching full-domain Authorship upper is thereby established. Core_initialize_block and BlockBuilder_finalize_block also enclose multiple owners; splitting into those calls does not authenticate phase attribution or equivalence to the selected single-call lifetime. Subtracting neighbour timings, restoring native callback-only boundaries or adding a host subscriber cannot close the missing boundary. Enabling Wasm tracing would change the artifact and still leave caller/glue and observation effects to qualify; it is not an allowed fallback in this closed inspection.

**Call-hook route rejection:** The separately inspected Wasmtime Store::call_hook route is rejected as a sufficient full Authorship I/F observer on pinned sc-executor-wasmtime0.47.0 / wasmtime36.0.14. Its four events are CallingWasm, ReturningFromWasm, CallingHost and ReturningFromHost: transitions between host and Wasm, not every internal Wasm function's entry/return or an Authorship phase identity. The actual call sites bracket host-to-guest invocation and guest-to-host imports. Host-call timestamps alone do not authenticate coverage of intervening Wasm work, complete I/F boundaries or caller registration/glue. This is a source-supported granularity refusal, not a missing-sample result.

**SDK attachment boundary:** InstanceWrapper owns a private Store; its store accessors are pub(crate), StoreData/Store are crate-private, and the public WasmInstance interface exposes export calls/allocation statistics rather than observer registration. Neither inspected sc-executor nor sc-executor-wasmtime source registers call_hook; the public Wasmtime executor configuration supplies no such callback. The upstream setter is call-hook feature-gated; no claim about the globally unified compiled feature set is needed for this refusal. Even exposing/enabling the hook would not add the missing internal phase events. No attachment, feature change, executor patch, tracing or sampling was attempted.

**Refusal scope and reopening:** Reject call_hook alone as the sufficient collector, not all possible VM observers or every future source-qualified reconstruction. Reopening this route needs new source-supported complete owner-boundary attribution, including registration/glue and observer effects; merely wiring the existing transition callback or collecting more host-call points does not provide it. Clock/error, domains, original-input/consumer coverage and host applicability would still require their own qualification. This documentation capture reuses the closed read-only inspection and rechecks only source identities; no independent execution or new physical method is claimed.

**Applicability limit and reopening:** Direct measurement of the actual chosen Wasm would remove native-to-Wasm time domination for that executed body, not clock/error, admitted-domain, proof-coordinate, complete ownership or host applicability obligations. The selected replay uses Onchain import=true with RecordingProofSizeProvider; the executor selects its import heap strategy via double(). That is not an attested PVF/default validation-host profile or Cumulus size-only equivalence. A separately selected route needs a source-supported full I/F VM observation boundary on the immutable artifact, or an explicitly qualified changed-carrier transfer, before a physical collector can be admitted. No build, Wasm execution, samples, tool installation, coefficient, provider or reserve change is authorized by this verdict.

## Dependency Coordination Family Proposal

Source audit: lib.rs::execute_mandatory_prepass already owns reserve→finite meter→dependency_scan_source_probe→optional process_next_dependency_scan_unit→consumed→settle. Q is the probe declaration; U is component-wise max(member, completion). Its envelope is Q+U. Empty selector consumes Q and releases U; every positive probe consumes Q+U even for completion. The worker charges U before its storage transaction and rolls back failed source/registration/Pending mutations, not its meter. Probe or worker errors become ResourceProtocolFailed before settlement/Service/publication. No free probe, actual-branch discount, extra unit, callback caching, fee or new physical owner follows.

Existing controls already record the actual probe and worker, not missing machinery. Positive dependency_scan_source_probe seeds only cursor/count, so is not a whole-worker topology producer. process_dependency_scan_unit resolves a balance source, publicly creates a Mutable System Actor with parked-balance activation, publishes a revision and records the real worker. process_dependency_scan_completion_unit deliberately seeds a standalone zero-length revision/source carrier without public balance registration; it proves that prepared primitive point, not registered Actor history. All use Weight::MAX and omit parent ledger reservation/settlement. Existing wide Close/temporal helpers also prepare real member/handoff histories; their broad populations are not required for this minimal wrapper family.

Proposed minimal service_prepass_dependency_scan(state, budget, envelope) returns only the existing consumed Weight. It shares the literal original parent block, with no new checks, receipts, scheduler entrypoint or typed outcome. Proposed mandatory_prepass_dependency_control(c) is exact/extra/raw-only and has three successful native source classes, not a price or maximum:

| c | Source preparation / required predicate | Successful verifier / booked Control delta |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Actual healthy empty selector after real prefix and Deadline prelude; fail closed if unavailable, never clear or drain reference sources to manufacture it | Empty selector retained, no worker-owned source change; Q |
| 1 | Reuse the existing real member setup producer; authoritative selector must be the unmodified singleton for the new source, fixed target has one live registration and no destination yet | Exact actor/source/revision Pending event, registration acknowledged and cursor advanced once; Q+U |
| 2 | Same real producer, exactly one real member unit in setup advances to cursor=end with revision=target; no synthetic completion seed or forced cursor | Existing event/registration retained, target cleared, source removed and selector empty through actual worker completion; Q+U |

Extract only that existing member setup producer for a second consumer; preserve all existing recorded bodies/verifier tails and completion/probe fixtures. New source classes require canonical topology/try_state checks and explicit supported-host predicates. Preparation is not an authenticated/admitted block history and must not claim two units in one legal Prepass. Failure to select the intended source or to construct exact completion is BenchmarkError::Stop, not permission to replace the head, clear peers, add adaptive work or invent chronology. Real begin_mandatory_prepass and service_prepass_deadlines run outside the recorded block before the new boundary; snapshot after that prelude, preserving any real preceding mutations. Peer Deadline outcomes stay opaque.

Successful cells reconcile local phase/budget, unchanged effect use, no outstanding reservation, unpublished canonical resource state and exact Q versus Q+U delta. Source/Actor semantic invariants and untouched unrelated state are verified outside recording; selected singleton removal must produce the exact empty selector. Refusal is a separate diagnostic/native obligation: malformed selector or admitted worker fault must remain ResourceProtocolFailed, public FRAME rollback must preserve its storage prefix, and private borrowed-ledger error cells must not claim memory restoration or settlement. No corrupt-source raw sample or production-reachable history is inferred. Existing carrier/member rollback tests are not themselves public-parent/local-ledger proof.

Native SDK plan: c0..2 × two real parent contexts × verify±, correct shared metadata oracle using DependencyScanSourceListState namespace evidence, identical saved body proof and positive verifier-read separation; do not interpret times/root fields. Shapes are finite success controls only. Empty/member/completion omission, callback/order changes, ledger deltas, failed metadata oracle or constructibility refusal are falsifiers, not occasions for coefficient/margin repairs. Full stale/reclamation/handoff/destination/max-geometry domain, error qualification, default/benchmark transfer, original/overlay lineage, complete P/D and shared Service/tail remain excluded. Existing Q and U declarations stay; any future inclusive replacement must retire contained additions and duplicate glue. No extraction or collection is performed by this proposal.
